newsitem.title: UK: Bookmaker says U.S. race is "almost a no contest".
newsitem.headline: Bookmaker says U.S. race is "almost a no contest".

text.p: A British bookmaker said on Thursday it had stopped taking bets on U.S. President Bill Clinton winning re-election in a race that it described as "almost a no contest".
Ladbrokes, one of Britain's biggest betting groups, gave Clinton a 1-10 chance of victory in the November 5 poll -- a bet of 10 pounds would produce only one pound profit.
His Republican challenger Bob Dole was a long way behind with odds of 6-1 and Ross Perot of the Reform Party was a distant third at 50-1.
"The U.S. presidential race is almost a no contest. You would be hard pressed to find a more one-sided two-horse race," Ladbrokes spokesman Simon Clare said in a statement.
"We have been taking a lot of money on Dole and Perot in recent weeks from customers hoping the election race will develop into a close-run event. With just days to go, that now looks doubtful."
